articles.body: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Joseph BAHOUT, Director, Issam Fares Institute for Public Policy & International Affairs. Despite the symbolism of a seventh round of US-sponsored negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, Bahout argues that the process is increasingly characterised by stagnation rather than diplomatic momentum. He suggests that the core obstacles are no longer merely technical disagreements over the implementation of the June framework agreement, but a convergence of military realities, domestic political constraints, diminishing American engagement, and wider regional tensions. The negotiations, in his view, exist within a broader strategic ecosystem in which progress on Lebanese-Israeli arrangements remains contingent upon developments in the Iran-US war and Israeli domestic politics.
articles.headline: Israel-Lebanon negotiations 'stalling': 'Situation on ground far from spirit of framework agreement'

articles.body: Camille Knight is pleased to welcome Dirk Segaar, IFRC Special Envoy for Sudan. Sudan's humanitarian crisis has become one of the defining yet least visible crises of the twenty first century. Segaar argues that the conflict can no longer be understood merely through the lens of shifting frontlines or military developments. Rather, he presents a picture of systemic societal collapse, in which war has hollowed out public services, displaced entire communities, accelerated disease, and created conditions where humanitarian need extends far beyond the active battlefields. Sudan is not simply a conflict zone but a nation experiencing the cumulative breakdown of its social, economic and institutional fabric.
articles.headline: 'World's largest humanitarian crisis Thirty five million Sudanese need humanitarian assistance'

articles.body: Progressives didn’t get the earthquake they expected. Moderates are relishing in their stronger than expected showing. In the early hours of Wednesday morning, with Michigan’s marquee Democratic Senate primary still in limbo, one of Democrats’ key questions of the midterms remains unresolved: Can the party’s most progressive faction successfully compete — and go on to win — in a battleground state? The razor-thin margin between progressive Abdul El-Sayed and moderate Rep. Haley Stevens will leave Democrats arguing about the answer regardless of who ultimately prevails. The finger-pointing within the party has already begun . “These guys are unbelievably cocky,” said a Democratic operative granted anonymity to speak candidly. The person was frustrated over El-Sayed’s decision to attend a pool party with progressive streamer Hasan Piker on Monday, hours before polls opened. El-Sayed led by three points by the time both candidates addressed their supporters around 1 a.m. Wednesday, with thousands of votes yet to be counted. He performed best in the state’s wealthiest and most highly-educated places, while Stevens outperformed him in areas with lower average incomes and where fewer voters have college degrees. But that marginal lead was a far cry from what El-Sayed and his allies had expected. Public polling in the campaign’s closing stretch showed El-Sayed ahead of Stevens by double digits. And his campaign projected confidence they would deliver a decisive win that would cement the strength of the progressive movement in Michigan, a state crucial to the Democratic Party’s prospects of retaking the Senate in November and, eventually, the White House in 2028. The progressive wave never materialized on Tuesday night, igniting fresh questions about the potency of the movement. Progressive candidates have notched a series of wins throughout the spring primary season in safe and competitive districts, from California to Maine. Michigan, however, was widely viewed as their biggest test yet. “The Democratic Party is a coalition that spans everything from center to socialist,” Democratic strategist Tré Easton wrote on social media Wednesday morning in response to Tuesday’s results. “Each part needs the other.” El-Sayed has maintained a steady lead after the polls closed, and could very well still pull off a win for his progressive coalition and advance to the general election — but instead of kicking off the next phase of his campaign with a victory lap, he’ll emerge limping out of a closer-than-foretold primary. Even beyond the Senate race, the results were mixed: Progressive Sunrise Movement co-founder William Lawrence won his primary for Michigan’s 7th District, but largely because two more moderate candidates had split the vote. Democratic socialist Donavan McKinney is still locked in a tight race with incumbent Rep. Shri Thanedar for Michigan’s 13th District. And over in Missouri, progressive Cori Bush’s comeback bid fell apart . “Bottom line is if [El-Sayed] wins, the DSA brand beyond major urban areas is not popular,” a national Democratic operative granted anonymity to speak candidly said early Wednesday morning. “Certainly puts a dent in the movement especially with Cori Bush’s loss.” Stevens sent her own supporters home on an optimistic note Wednesday morning: “I’m feeling good about this race.” El-Sayed, for his part, quickly recast his narrow lead as a victory against the barrage of spending against him from pro-Stevens groups — despite projecting enough confidence to declare he would beat Rogers “by seven” percentage points in the general election earlier on Tuesday. “I wish I could tell you that I was declaring victory right about now. Turns out it takes a long time to count some votes in Michigan,” El-Sayed told supporters at his election night party in Detroit. For some El-Sayed allies a win is a win, even if the final margins are close. “Any win is good, as long as it’s called tonight,” Bhaskar Sunkara, a 2020 Bernie Sanders surrogate and former DSA vice chair, told POLITICO . Regardless of the final outcome, the race’s narrow margin ensures that the winner will have significant work to do to unify the party after an acrimonious primary riddled with personal attacks from both sides — a reality both candidates appeared to acknowledge in remarks to supporters. “To all of our supporters here tonight, watching on TV, tomorrow we begin to mend fences,” El-Sayed said. “If your instinct is to be like, 'I told you.' Nope. Let's come together to build a movement that's even bigger, that's even stronger, that's even more powerful, that reaches into the very depths of this state, that reminds us the best of who we are and who we can be.” Democrats across the state had already set their focus on uniting their deeply fractured party ahead of another likely bruising contest in the general election. “It’s no secret that this has at once been a contentious and bruising primary, but Democrats through it all have shown resilience towards coming together following primaries,” said Chris Herweyer, an organizing director for the Kent County Democratic Party. Michigan State Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who ran for Senate before suspending her campaign a month before the primary, endorsed El-Sayed early Wednesday as he maintained a narrow advantage over Rep. Haley Stevens — another sign of swift efforts to reconcile, even as the race remained in limbo. Republicans, meanwhile, are still hoping for an El-Sayed win. Rogers’ primary proved a bright spot for Republicans on the Senate map, where the party successfully avoided a costly and heated primary of their own and could focus early on the general election. “El-Sayed is the preferred candidate” for Republicans, Jason Roe, a longtime Republican operative in Michigan, said in a text message. “El-Sayed is not doing very well outstate and I think that’s what a lot of Republicans are banking on. It will be very difficult for him to beat Rogers with those rural counties.” Andrew Howard and Will Steakin contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Progressives didn’t get the big election night they wanted

articles.body: Two years after former Rep. Cori Bush told the American Israel Political Affairs Committee she’d be back to “tear your kingdom down,” voters in Missouri’s 1st District again rejected her staunch criticisms of Israel and AIPAC. Rep. Wesley Bell (D-Mo.), who unseated Bush in a 2024 primary after she became one of the first members of Congress to call the Israel's actions in Gaza in its war with Hamas a "genocide," trounced the former member of "the Squad” on Tuesday night by a yawning margin. It’s a snag for Democratic progressives who have otherwise seen a slew of primary wins campaigning on ending military aid for Israel, and who have sought to make support from AIPAC into political poison. The race had some key differences from when they squared off two years ago. An AIPAC-backed super PAC still spent $2 million boosting Bell, but that was a far cry from the $9.3 million the group spent two years ago, according to data from ad tracker AdImpact. And Bush got no backup this year on the airwaves from the constellation of progressive groups that rallied to her cause in 2024. The size of Bell’s victory suggests that Democratic primary voters' anger toward politicians who remain supportive of Israel isn't limitless, despite public sentiment nationwide broadly moving against Israel . Bell, who has affirmed support for Israel’s relationship with the United States, beat Bush by about six points in 2024 and appears on track to win by even more. On Tuesday night, AIPAC reposted a POLITICO story about the fight over AIPAC in the district, writing simply: "Congratulations, Wesley Bell!" Bell also enjoyed the backing of establishment Democrats this year, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and the Congressional Black Caucus PAC. Bush on the other hand, solidified her progressive bonafides with endorsements from Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and the Democratic Socialists of America.
articles.headline: Progressives' anti-AIPAC wave hits a snag in St. Louis

articles.body: South Dakota Democratic Senate nominee Julian Beaudion dropped out of the race Tuesday, a move that comes following heightened pressure from within the party to clear the way for a stronger independent candidate, according to paperwork filed with the South Dakota Secretary of State’s office . Beaudion’s decision comes on the same day as the deadline to withdraw, and just days after he told POLITICO he was not going to leave the race. Now, independent Brian Bengs will face a one-on-one battle with Republican Sen. Mike Rounds in November. In a statement, Beaudion likened his decision to the failed Apollo 13 mission to the moon. “It is with a tremendous amount of gratitude to everyone who has supported our campaign mission and a great amount of sorrow, that I say, ‘Houston, we have a problem,’” he wrote. Beaudion is the third Democrat in a deep-red Senate race who has left in order to give independents — who have polled better and raised more money — a better shot at defeating Republicans. Already, Democrats in Idaho and Nebraska have dropped out and endorsed independents. But Montana Democrat Alani Bankhead has steadfastly insisted she will not suspend her campaign for the better-funded independent Seth Bodnar in what otherwise could be the best shot for an independent candidate to knock off a red-state Republican this fall. Bengs, a former Democrat who was crushed by Majority Leader John Thune when he ran for Senate in 2022, has touted internal polling showing a competitive race with Rounds — but only if Beaudion exited.
articles.headline: South Dakota Democrat exits Senate race, clears way for independent

articles.body: The battle to become the country’s next progressive leader in the mold of Bernie Sanders is heating up ahead of Democrats’ direction-defining Michigan Senate primary. Nowhere is the jockeying and strategy unfolding behind the scenes more pronounced than between Democratic Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and Ro Khanna of California, who have taken disparate approaches to the midterms as they build out their political brands. Khanna’s go-everywhere mentality versus Ocasio-Cortez’s more selective involvement in key races this cycle will test their political acumen and relationships, potentially setting them up for a 2028 presidential race that could decide who will inherit the movement. In much of Sanders’ inner circle, who comes next is pretty obvious, even as the wider progressive movement continues to clash over the answer. “It’s always been clear that AOC is the heir,” one person close to Sanders who’s been involved in such conversations with him for years, granted anonymity to share their understanding of the private discussions. “Always.” Yet within the broader Sanders coalition, there is plenty of behind-the-scenes posturing — and outright bickering — over who will ultimately take over for the Vermont senator. Khanna’s allies say Ocasio-Cortez is playing it too safe to be the next standard-bearer, with some prominent left-wing leaders irked by her sparing endorsement strategy. Ocasio-Cortez’s and Khanna’s diverging paths are on full display in Michigan , where Democrats’ most contentious Senate primary is coming to a head Tuesday in a critical battleground that will have outsized importance in selecting Democrats’ next presidential nominee. Both representatives and Sanders have backed Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official who has surged in polls against establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens as he consolidates support among the left. But only Ocasio-Cortez has appeared alongside Sanders in stumping for El-Sayed, with the two holding a joint rally in Lansing, Michigan, last month. Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders are featured prominently in one of El-Sayed’s closing television ads, in a key sign of who the campaign thinks can best help push him over the finish line. Khanna, meanwhile, cut a separate digital fundraising appeal for El-Sayed and has campaigned for him without Sanders. Sanders and Khanna do maintain a relationship — the California representative was a national co-chair of Sanders’ 2020 presidential bid — but there’s doubt within the Vermont independent’s orbit over how successful a Khanna presidential run would be or whether he's best positioned to inherit the progressive throne, should Ocasio-Cortez choose not to run for president in 2028. "Ro is basically already running, but not many are taking him too seriously as the movement's next leader," said another operative close to Sanders, granted anonymity to speak candidly. In an interview, Khanna brushed off the notion that there's a single heir to the Vermont senator’s progressive movement. "I believe that Sanders is going to have many successors over decades, and the key is to build a majoritarian progressivism that can win across the country," he said. Asked whether an Ocasio-Cortez presidential bid would change his calculus, he answered flatly: "No." His decision, he says, will come “around Thanksgiving.” A representative for Ocasio-Cortez declined to comment. Sanders, for his part, is trying to rise above the jockeying. “The presidential election is in 2 years and 3 months,” Sanders said in a statement. “Let’s focus now on how we resolve the urgent issues facing our country. There is plenty of time to worry about possible presidential candidates.” Why Sanders world sees AOC as the successor Sanders, 84, and Ocasio-Cortez, 36, share a deeply personal bond their advisers say transcends politics but remains rooted in their shared ideals. They talk directly about key policy, political ideas and candidates to boost, and they even coordinated their endorsements around a group of New York democratic socialists and progressives who ultimately won House seats. The two also share a circle of advisers, including Faiz Shakir and Mike Casca. Casca, a former long-time Sanders aide, now serves as Ocasio-Cortez’s chief of staff and plays a major role in shaping policy and political strategy. Shakir is an adviser to Sanders and executive director of More Perfect Union, a progressive nonprofit media organization. “I’m sure there are a lot of people who are interested in being the next Bernie Sanders, I think he’d be less inclined to give them his endorsement” over Ocasio-Cortez, said a third person close to Sanders, who’s been involved in the conversations around his political and policy strategy for years, granted anonymity to discuss them. Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez have approached the midterms differently. The Vermont independent has worked to expand his endorsement roster and his presence on the campaign trail this year, which his allies see as an effort to cultivate a lasting generation of progressive leaders to carry on his movement. He often endorses early, acting as a validator for left-leaning candidates’ campaigns and platforms, while Ocasio-Cortez has been serving as more of a closer. It’s a strategic shift for the New York Democrat, who used to get involved in races earlier — a calculus advisers say is a recognition of her ability to mobilize certain voting blocs, like communities of color and working-class voters, late in the game. They don’t coordinate on every contest, but they have joined forces in several races — including El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate race and Sam Forstag’s House primary in Montana. Ocasio-Cortez called Sanders as soon as she decided to endorse El-Sayed and they immediately began planning a rally for him, according to a person familiar with the discussions and granted anonymity to describe the private conversations. Earlier this year, Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez together also developed the leading progressive push to address artificial intelligence. Sanders was the first member of Congress to call for an AI moratorium, and he helped shape Ocasio-Cortez’s stance. The pair unveiled joint legislation in March to ban the rapid build up of data center construction. Months later, the issue is now cutting across progressive and conservative voting blocs, is a preeminent policy issue on Capitol Hill and is at the heart of dozens of midterm races and even early 2028 presidential talk. “Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and I understand what is at stake,” Sanders said as he introduced the AI moratorium bill alongside the New York Democrat this spring in the Senate. Progressive candidates whose campaigns have received nods from both Ocasio-Cortez and Khanna say they are both key validators who carry different appeal. Khanna has risen in prominence because of his push to release files on Jeffrey Epstein. And Ocasio-Cortez brings the kind of star power and nationalized spotlight that campaigns say is invaluable for growing candidates’ exposure, particularly among younger progressive voters who can be trickier to turn out. “AOC’s very popular, she has a lot of grassroots support … all across the country,” said Adam Hamawy, who was endorsed by both representatives in his New Jersey House primary this spring. “Ro Khanna has not just progressives, but he’s had a strong stance against corruption. … There’s a lot of overlap but each of them have specific things that come together to paint a wider picture than if I just had one.” Don’t count Ro out yet Not everyone around Sanders is sold on Ocasio-Cortez as the heir apparent. Khanna allies argue he's the one who has been putting in the work — and sticking his neck out for the progressive movement — by backing primary challengers to incumbents, getting out front on issues like the Epstein files, and recently traveling to the West Bank. “People who are supporting her are supporting her more as a brand," said one Khanna ally and Sanders world operative, granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. "What does it mean to work with her? What does it mean for her to pass a bill? I don't know her theory of change." There is fear Ocasio-Cortez is "weirdly isolating herself" over the years ahead of a 2028 decision, the operative added. "I could not tell you who AOC's advisers are at this point [beyond Casca]. If you're thinking of running for president, you want to be in an expansive, elevated, exciting space, not in a controlled environment.” Ocasio-Cortez has been significantly more selective in her endorsements than either Khanna or Sanders, backing left-wing candidates across several competitive House primaries but steering clear of some of the messiest contests on the map, including Maine Senate and Wisconsin’s imploding gubernatorial primary. That approach has drawn consternation from some on the left who say she’s playing it too safe given her political cachet, particularly as she declines to join other progressives in endorsing against incumbents — notably in her own backyard — even though that’s how she won her seat in 2018. “Who cares about your win-loss ratio? What I care about is, are you trying to help fellow progressives or aren’t you?” said Cenk Uygur, a Khanna supporter who founded the progressive online network “The Young Turks” and Justice Democrats. “AOC cares so much about her colleagues, and her colleagues are establishment Democrats. I don’t care about them. In fact, I’m opposed to them,” Uygur added. “I want them challenged in primaries.” Khanna has worked to keep his own close ties to Sanders and his circle. Jeff Weaver, Sanders’ 2016 campaign manager, now serves as a senior adviser to Khanna as he’s pushing to be a high-profile progressive leader and laying the framework for a possible 2028 presidential run. “No two candidates are equal,” Weaver said. “But I think Ro Khanna has the chance to do what Bernie did, which is to have appeal beyond the Democratic base.” Khanna has spent years trying to build the kind of early-state infrastructure a presidential campaign requires, traveling to early primary and battleground states to lay the organizational groundwork for a potential run. Since 2021, he has been working to assemble steering committees of 75 to 100 people in New Hampshire and Nevada, with another being built in South Carolina, while working with local political power players, according to Shannon Jackson, another longtime Sanders operative who is now consulting for Khanna. Over the last week, the California representative has been on what he is calling an "new economic patriotism tour" through Pennsylvania, holding events in counties Trump carried like Erie, Luzerne and Cambria "There is a great desire for a bold, progressive vision that is going to call out an unfair and rigged political and economic system," he told POLITICO. But the test, Khanna argued, is making that vision work "not just in the Bay Area, not just in Michigan, not just in progressive areas, but in places like Pennsylvania." Khanna has endorsed dozens of candidates up and down the ballot this year, wading into some of the most fraught Democratic House, Senate and gubernatorial primaries in the country. That widespread involvement has produced a mixed track record with some high-profile losses, including Graham Platner’s disgraced exit from Maine’s Senate primary and Tom Steyer’s expensive loss in the California governor’s race. In the case of Platner, Khanna and Sanders endorsed the Maine progressive, while Ocasio-Cortez, notably, stayed out of the race altogether. Khanna also has backed candidates against the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and establishment. For example, Khanna-endorsed progressive Matt Dunlap in Maine’s 2nd Congressional District successfully defeated the DCCC’s preferred candidate. “There’s a difference between being a progressive in policies and being a progressive in action,” said Uygur. “And action requires you challenging the system, challenging the establishment. On those grounds, it’s not close. Ro Khanna is head and shoulders above every other Democrat.”
articles.headline: Bernie Sanders’ circle is pretty clear on who his successor will be

articles.body: Cori Bush’s 2024 primary loss to Wesley Bell was heralded as a major defeat for the insurgent progressive movement. Now, their rematch for Missouri’s 1st District two years later comes at a time when Bush and her allies seem to be winning the battle for the future of the Democratic Party. The dueling factions in St. Louis highlight the growing tension over not just the domestic ideological divide in the Democratic Party, but the party’s — and country’s — stance on the U.S.'s longrunning relationship with Israel. The former representative was among the first sitting members of Congress to call Israel's actions in Gaza a "genocide" — and now she's betting that her progressive bonafides and her criticism of the top U.S. ally will boost her to victory with the same electorate that punished her last cycle. “One of us is of the people, by the people and for the people,” Bush said in a recent interview. “The other one is paid for by AIPAC. That's the difference.” Like two years ago, a group aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee is the largest outside spender in the race. The organization’s super PAC, United Democracy Project, has spent at least $2.1 million on advertising in the primary, according to ad tracking firm AdImpact. Roughly half of all adults who identify as Democrats believe that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians, according to a July AP-NORC poll , an accusation that some human rights organizations have made but both the Israeli and American governments strongly deny. And from Colorado to New York, several progressives have already tapped into voters' frustrations with party leadership and successfully wielded their criticism of Israel's government in order to win. St. Louis is only one of several races on Tuesday testing the Democratic Party’s establishment: voters will also hit the polls in Michigan to cast their ballots for the progressive, Abdul El-Sayed, or the moderate Rep. Haley Stevens for an open Senate seat. That race has also become a check for voters’ opposition to AIPAC. And some potential 2028 Democratic contenders have already sworn off accepting funding from AIPAC, another sign of the growing unwillingness to be aligned with the organization. AIPAC and some Democrats have hit back, saying its critics within the Democratic Party have increasingly made the party inhospitable to those generally supportive of Israel. In response to requests for comment, AIPAC shared a series of ads knocking Bush for her missed votes and her criticism of the Biden administration and former Vice President Kamala Harris’s 2024 presidential bid. (In a recent debate, Bush claimed Bell delayed his endorsement of Harris, but both endorsed the former vice president on July 21, 2024 , the same day she announced her candidacy.) Bell unseated Bush two years ago with heavy financial backing from AIPAC, the country’s preeminent pro-Israel lobby. They’ve once again spent heavily on his behalf, and this time, he also comes into the race with establishment support — including endorsements from House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and the Congressional Black Caucus PAC. Bell and his allies have absolutely swamped Bush on the airwaves this year. In addition to UDP’s $2.1 million in ad spending, Bell’s campaign has followed closely behind at over $2 million, according to AdImpact, with over $700,000 more from another super PAC called New Democrat Majority. Bush, meanwhile, has spent less than $200,000, according to the ad tracker. She boasts the backing of a progressive coalition that includes the Democratic Socialists of America, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and fellow "Squad" member Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.). Bell has brushed aside the attacks that he’s being bolstered by AIPAC money. “I think we all can agree that there's too much money in politics, and I'm a vocal and public supporter of campaign finance reform,” Bell said in an interview. “What I'm not a fan of or a supporter of is singling out certain Americans and saying that they should not participate in our democratic process. That is where I would absolutely draw the line.” Bell added that the difference between himself and Bush is that he can offer both support and criticism of allies. “While I’m not the biggest fan of [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu], I still believe that we have to stand with our allies,” Bell said. “That doesn't mean we're not going to disagree at times with our allies.” Bell’s and Bush’s showdown in 2024 was arguably the biggest ideological battlefield for the party that year, outside of the discontent surrounding Biden and then Harris’ presidential bids from progressives critical of Israel. But two years later, it is just one of many fights that has sprawled across the country. Progressive candidates have been racking up primary victories against establishment figures in a trend that some are calling the “Mamdani effect” after democratic socialist New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani took down Andrew Cuomo in both the 2025 primary and general elections. Still, this year’s St. Louis rematch isn’t quite the marquee fight it was in 2024. Spending has trended down: Collectively nearly $20 million was dropped on the 2024 contest on advertising, according to AdImpact. That’s roughly four times more than this year’s total. Usamah Andrabi, spokesperson for Justice Democrats, the progressive group that endorsed Bush earlier this cycle, attributed the broader, nationwide ideological fight to a base that has been “pushed to the edge of desperation by the Democratic Party itself.” “The Democratic Party’s base woke up in January 2025 realizing that their party's establishment was unfit, unprepared and frankly unwilling to fight back against Donald Trump and Republican extremists with the urgency the moment demanded,” Andrabi said. Now, as St. Louis voters head to the polls on Tuesday, Bush cast the eventual outcome in dire terms. “What is at stake,” Bush said, “is the affordability and the peace of every single person in this country.”
articles.headline: Democrats’ stance on Israel takes center stage in Bush-Bell rematch in St. Louis

articles.body: Michigan Republicans haven’t had a better shot to win the governorship in over a decade. Deciding who should take it is turning into an ugly, hyper-online brawl. With widespread name recognition and an endorsement from President Donald Trump, Rep. John James appears poised to be the GOP nominee ahead of Michigan’s primary Tuesday. But the West Point graduate once thought of as a rising star within the national GOP is facing stiff resistance from an outspoken grassroots wing of the state party, which is rallying around his sole remaining competitor. “I think you're gonna be surprised when this race comes down,” said Oakland County GOP Chair Vance Patrick, who endorsed businessperson-turned-outsider candidate Perry Johnson in the closing weeks of the race. “It's getting really interesting.” As James and Johnson careen toward a contest to decide who faces likely Democratic nominee and current Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, the campaigning is getting weird. Johnson has launched increasingly caustic and personal attacks against James, who has led the field since he entered the race. And Johnson cuts an odd figure for a leading contender: He is perhaps best known for his quixotic 2024 presidential bid, which came after a 2022 gubernatorial campaign fell apart amid a nominating petition scandal . But state party officials and grassroots activists have also shared publicly and privately a litany of complaints about James: resentment over too many debates missed early on in the campaign, not enough visits to specific parts of the state, frustration over him giving away a battleground House seat Democrats are targeting this cycle to run for a new job after losing two previous statewide elections. Nonetheless, even his detractors insist that Republican voters will rally around the eventual nominee. Patrick, whose county party — which includes parts of metro Detroit that fall within James’ district — received $13,350 from the Johnson campaign, said Republicans “will join lockstep behind the guy that wins the primary.” The intra-party consternation comes at a pivotal moment for Michigan Republicans, who’ve watched eight years of Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer’s leadership — and yawning statewide victories — with disdain. Meanwhile, Democrats appear ready to elevate Benson, who has built a $6.4 million war chest as of mid-July — albeit dwarfed by Johnson’s personal wealth — thanks to a prolific fundraising advantage . The secretary of state appears to be en route to easily beat Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson for the nomination. And Trump winning the state in 2024 is no assurance for Republicans, who saw their Senate candidate falter to now-Sen. Elissa Slotkin in the same year. Now, the GOP is facing an uphill battle amid rising gas prices brought on by a deeply unpopular war in Iran that is causing headaches for the party nationwide. Finding a nominee who can win over independents and compete in the mother of all swing states is paramount, some Republicans say, and they’re not sure James is it. “There’s a large amount of Republicans that do not like him,” said Hassan Nehme, a former vice chair of the Michigan GOP and current candidate for state Legislature, referring to some voters’ hesitance about James’ voting record. The Johnson campaign has launched vitriolic personal attacks at James throughout the race. Johnson, who is white, has referred to James, one of the few Black Republicans in Congress and the sole Black candidate in the race, as a “ DEI candidate ,” and accused him of playing the “ race card ” during a recent debate. James, in turn, has characterized Johnson as “ desperate .” The campaign has also turned to promoting an unsubstantiated rumor, while providing no evidence, about James’ personal life, reposting social media posts that attack James. Tori Sachs, a senior adviser for the James campaign, characterized Johnson’s attacks in a statement as “lies” that are exposing “a desperate, career candidate who has no grasp on reality and no friends that he didn’t buy.” "Never-Trumper Perry Johnson has burned through over $70 million attacking Trump and James with lies, only to crash toward his third loss in three cycles,” she said. Such plays are emblematic of Johnson’s campaign strategy, which has leaned heavily online and embraced a constituency of right-leaning grassroots organizers. On social media, he’s employed artificial intelligence to construct sometimes bizarre ads, including a six-minute long odyssey in which he doggedly pursues James on foot, bus and helicopter in order to debate him. Brian Szmytke, a campaign spokesperson for the Johnson campaign, reiterated in a statement that “John James is unelectable in a general election,” listing several attacks levied during the campaign. The scrappy turn in the campaign intensified when former state Attorney General Mike Cox, who was also courting voters skeptical of the GOP establishment, dropped out of the race in mid-July. But even before then, Republican officials across the state had expressed doubts about James. That the Johnson campaign has attacked James on such personal terms points to the campaign’s dire straits, said John Sellek, a Michigan-based Republican political consultant. “We’ve turned a corner since Cox got out, where the Perry Johnson campaign has been throwing haymakers on what look like less than prime issues because they know the end is here,” Sellek said. That’s all despite a huge spending advantage for the self-funding Johnson. He has spent over $32 million getting on the airwaves, while James’ campaign has spent $2.4 million, according to advertising insight firm AdImpact. “All the typical support mechanisms are moving toward James, even though he is being wildly outspent,” said Sellek. Before appearing in a set of televised debates held in July, James had abstained from participating in several debates held earlier in the primary. James at the time defended skipping the events, saying he was more focused on uniting the party than bickering with candidates. But some voters took his absence as a sign of disengagement from the grassroots. Daire Rendon — the Republican Party chair for Michigan’s 1st District, which covers the entire Upper Peninsula and swaths of northern Michigan — suggested that James doesn’t connect with voters in her rural region. Rendon, a former state representative who was charged for her alleged involvement in a scheme to unlawfully access voting machines after the 2020 election, noted that “we don’t see John James much.” “They are going to gravitate towards candidates who spend time learning about [the Upper Peninsula], and who show up,” said Rendon, who pleaded not guilty and whose case is ongoing. Detractors have also criticized James for running for governor in the first place, viewing the contested House seat he’s leaving behind as more valuable amid the GOP’s slim majority and as Republicans stare down an unfavorable midterm cycle. Trump also initially took issue with his gubernatorial ambitions, grousing about it publicly, before endorsing him in June. “You don't blow off 80 million in an investment to get you elected to Congress, and in one term leave,” said Muskegon County GOP Chair Tim Cross. (James was first elected to the House in 2022.) James, however, also appears to have a slew of grassroots support himself. Several Michigan Republicans touted James in interviews with POLITICO, including former state legislator and Macomb County Prosecutor Peter Lucido, who said James is “a proven leader, and he’s gonna continue to go ahead and govern and lead.” Public and private polling appears to indicate that James remains comfortably in the lead. An internal poll , shared with POLITICO, of more than 700 likely primary voters conducted for the Cox campaign in the days before he dropped out in mid-July showed James leading with 36 percent points, with Johnson trailing at 23 percent and Cox at 21 percent. Likely Cox voters split for Johnson over James as their second choice, 44 percent to 38 percent respectively. James, the Cox campaign wrote in a memo to donors and supporters attached to the polling, “benefited by hundreds of millions of dollars targeted toward voters, specifically in Southeast Michigan, over the past several election cycles, coupled with the endorsement of President Donald Trump, creating a scenario where James’ lead is largely insulated.” Now, the James campaign is rolling out its line of endorsements ranging from state representatives, senators and conservative activists, with Trump’s endorsement as a crown jewel. The president brought James on stage at a late July rally outside Detroit, where the candidate asserted, falsely, for the first time that Trump won Michigan in 2020. James had previously said that Joe Biden won the 2020 election, though he said earlier this cycle that he was “ screwed ” that year when he lost his Senate bid. “You have to win,” the president told James onstage Monday. “You have to win.”
articles.headline: Michigan’s GOP governor primary is getting weird

articles.body: He’s eating barbecue. He’s winning over Joe Rogan. He’s challenging his opponent to mano-a-mano televised faceoffs. James Talarico is determined not to let his GOP challenger Ken Paxton’s and Republicans’ attacks on his masculinity define him in what has emerged as one of the party's loudest tactics in the crucial Senate race. The Texas Democrat is working to position himself as a candidate focused on issues he says men actually care about instead of speculation about his diet, sexuality and religious beliefs. "They've even called me a vegan, and those are fighting words in the state of Texas," Talarico said at a San Antonio rally this summer. “Nowadays our culture tells young men that greatness is tearing other people down, is trolling and owning and dominating. But my dad showed me what real greatness looks like. He inspired me to serve,” Talarico said at another rally in Houston, referencing how his dad often mowed the lawn of his elderly widowed neighbor without asking. Talarico’s attempt to reclaim the masculinity narrative by confronting the issue head-on could help propel him to flip a seat Democrats haven’t held in nearly four decades, and which could determine control of the Senate next year. It comes as both parties, in Texas and across the U.S., are fighting to win male voters — especially young , Black or Hispanic men — who in 2024 lurched to the right to help Republicans take control of the White House and Congress. The issue of masculinity has also been turbo-charged during Donald Trump’s second term, with the president hosting UFC fights on the White House lawn and his Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth pushing for testosterone testing in the military. If Talarico prevails, he could ultimately serve as a model for other Democratic candidates to connect with male voters or fend off Republicans who try to use issues of masculinity as a cudgel. “Democrats need to be prepared for more of these attacks to come and understand how to handle them,” Lucas Holtz, a senior political adviser at the centrist think tank Third Way, said in an interview. Republicans think they’ve hit a nerve with Texas voters about Talarico’s manhood. Members of the party have targeted the 37-year-old public school teacher-turned-state legislator for past statements endorsing a vegan lifestyle , suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and opposing legislation that erodes transgender rights. “If you look at him, this is a guy who’s publicly stated pretty bizarre things — that God is nonbinary,” said Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas) in an interview. “He’s a total weirdo, and I think Texas voters recognize that.” Talarico said recently his comment on God's gender was meant to be "deliberately provocative" and that he meant God is beyond gender. Republicans are also seizing on Talarico’s unmarried status and smaller physical build to paint the Democratic candidate as weak and effeminate. Some have falsely called him gay or transgender . Paxton’s very first ad of the general election campaign implied Talarico has low testosterone levels. And a conservative PAC released an AI-generated video of Talarico as an actress from “The Sound of Music” singing about wanting to give hormones to children. Talarico opposes gender affirming care for minors, his spokesperson JT Ennis said. “In Texas, there’s a certain level of tough guy-ness that we all pretend to have in ourselves, and that we like in our elected officials,” said Vinny Minchillo, a Texas-based Republican admaker who is not involved in the race. “If you push that the right direction, that especially does not sit well with Hispanic men and Black men.” Paxton’s campaign and his allies think Talarico’s previous comments on these issues put him out of touch with voters in both parties. “Texans can spot an audition for a new identity and they know he is weak and woke on core Texas values,” Paxton adviser Nick Maddux said in a statement. Maddux pointed to moves Talarico has made during the campaign he said shows flip-flopping, such as wearing a Texas flag shirt after calling the American flag a “complicated symbol.” “He is undoubtedly hurting Democrats,” Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz said in an interview about Talarico. Some Hill Democrats say Republicans’ fixation on Talarico’s manhood is an attempt to distract from Paxton’s weaknesses. “They fear his strength, especially since he’s running against the most notorious scumbag in American politics,” Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) said. Paxton has faced an ethics complaint that was later dropped, a Justice Department corruption investigation for which he was not charged and securities fraud charges which were ultimately dismissed in an agreement . He was also impeached by the Texas GOP-led House for bribery and abusing his public office, which he called a “sham” coordinated by liberals, and was later acquitted by the Texas Senate. Paxton also has a history of using cultural issues to his advantage, such as stoking anti-Muslim fears through campaign messaging . Meanwhile, Talarico’s campaign says they’re not seeing evidence that the masculinity barbs are gaining traction, pointing to robust Democratic gains among Hispanic voters while also arguing that polling shows a toss-up general election contest. The campaign did not share specific data to support that its messaging to male voters was lifting Talarico’s polling with that demographic. Talarico has focused on issues he says affect many men — like lowering housing costs, stopping corporate landlord rent manipulation and curbing the influence of billionaire mega-donors in politics. “Ken Paxton is picking these fights no one cares about to distract from the fact that he has no solutions to lower the cost of gas, groceries, or healthcare,” Ennis said in a statement. “Real men serve others, weak men serve themselves.” Talarico also has tried to appeal to young men and Hispanic voters by placing ads during World Cup and NBA Finals games. And he’s challenging Paxton to a series of televised debates, in which the two could spar on manhood and other issues. Paxton’s team said he’s agreed to the debates but they’re still negotiating logistics and terms. The Democrat’s campaign also said it is trying to facilitate similar opportunities to Talarico’s pivotal appearance on Joe Rogan’s podcast last year, which boosted his national profile to millions of young men who make up Rogan’s core audience. The podcaster — who during the interview exclaimed “you need to run for president,” to Talarico — has continued to compliment the Texas Democrat and defend his views, including during a conversation with Vice President JD Vance last month. Talarico has also fired back with his own jabs. He responded to Paxton calling him “Talafreako” by putting the phrase on T-shirts and selling them on his campaign website. And Talarico turned on Paxton’s low-testosterone message by telling MS NOW “I don’t think guys my age are really concerned about that kind of thing,” adding, “You’ve got these old guys lathered up in their fake tans throwing cheesy nicknames at each other." Some public opinion research shows Talarico’s strategy fits the 2026 moment. The growing cost-of-living crisis — exacerbated by the deeply unpopular military conflict in Iran — and Trump’s low approval ratings may mean the GOP’s masculinity attacks fall flat this cycle, Luke Warford, founder and director of Texas Public Opinion Research , a nonpartisan public opinion research firm, said in an interview. The top issues for men and young men in Texas center on affordability, the cost of living, economic growth and job creation, according to an aggregate of data shared with POLITICO from the group’s latest surveys in May and June. “We've got a really different scenario now where the Republicans are in power in Texas and nationally, so they own the things that are broken,” Warford said. “There is a deep anti-establishment sentiment in this country and a deep frustration with the status quo particularly among men, and that could be a much stronger political force than the cultural attacks.” Matt Angle, founder of the Lone Star Project, a Democratic-aligned political action committee in Texas, said “there’s no attack that should be ignored,” but that Democrats are in a good position. “Ken Paxton is no he-man. He’s a thin-chested, soft spoken, weak guy,” Angle said. One warning sign for Talarico: a swath of male voters perceive him as too progressive, said Holtz, the Third Way adviser. Holtz noted a recent poll of men by the group in which 49 percent of respondents said the candidate was “too far left.” In focus groups held by the centrist think tank last year and this year , young men overwhelmingly pointed to the Republican Party as the better representative of men’s priorities. Respondents in those groups associated Democrats with more social and cultural issues while tying Republicans with financial independence, finding a partner and starting a family. On Capitol Hill, some Democrats are calling the conversation in Texas an opportunity to revisit the party’s historic avoidance of issues that are important to men, which have made them more susceptible to criticism. Rep. Marc Veasey, a moderate Texas Democrat, said in an interview that “Democrats, overall, need to do a better job of expressing some of the concerns that young men have.” “When we have people on our side who are attacking things like nuclear family structure and expecting everybody to fall in line, that’s pure insanity,” Veasey said. “There’s this expectation with Democrats that men are just going to follow along, and they’re not. We haven’t figured out how to talk to them.” Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) said in an interview that Democrats tend to display examples of “traditional masculinity” rather than the “stereotypical masculinity” Republicans are attacking them for not adhering to. He pointed out he served in the Marines, Sen. Cory Booker (D-N.J.) played football and Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) was an astronaut. “What voters know is truly masculine is a politician who is going to take care of their needs and be a protector and be a provider for the family,” Gallego added. “When a man can’t support his family because inflation is so fucking high, they’re not going to care about who is on the ballot that is, quote unquote, ‘not masc enough.’”

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/BF3HY7H72NA2NBGIYU7YVZBF5M.JPG?auth=4805b082611de771718399d77dc7eb697c536bb81669c798d60b1091fb846cc3" width="6000" height="4000" alt="Entrada del antiguo hospital militar de Ceuta, este martes."></img><p>Una gran habitación diáfana a -5° es el espacio que han terminado ocupando los cuerpos de las 77 personas que perdieron la vida el jueves en la última entrada multitudinaria de migrantes desde Marruecos por <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/marlaska-insiste-en-que-el-cni-no-alerto-de-una-llegada-masiva-de-migrantes-a-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/marlaska-insiste-en-que-el-cni-no-alerto-de-una-llegada-masiva-de-migrantes-a-ceuta.html">el espigón fronterizo de Ceuta</a> y cuyos cadáveres fueron recuperados en el lado español de la frontera. Un intenso olor invade el lugar, mantienen quienes han trabajado allí estos días. “Ni respirando con lentitud se alivia”, afirman. Conforme pasa el tiempo, el cerebro lo atenúa y pasa a segundo plano. La magnitud de esta tragedia, en la que el ansia por salir del agua hizo que muchas de las personas terminaran escalando sobre otras y hundiéndolas en el mar, activó el protocolo para grandes catástrofes con víctimas múltiples. El antiguo hospital militar de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/esto-no-es-torre-pacheco-la-estrategia-fallida-de-la-ultraderecha-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/esto-no-es-torre-pacheco-la-estrategia-fallida-de-la-ultraderecha-en-ceuta.html">Ceuta,</a> un complejo castrense con varios edificios, terminó convirtiéndose en una gran morgue en cuestión de horas. Y se creó un gabinete de crisis, formado por forenses del Instituto de Medicina Legal y agentes del Servicio de Criminalística y de la Comandancia de la Guardia Civil de Ceuta, en el que también colaboraron militares.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-05/un-hangar-a-5-para-custodiar-a-los-77-fallecidos-que-dejo-la-avalancha-de-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Un hangar a -5° para custodiar a los 77 fallecidos que dejó la avalancha de Ceuta

articles.body: <p>Descalificaciones “impropias” de un juez, peticiones “atípicas” o comentarios “intimidatorios”. Las quejas enviadas por el ministro Félix Bolaños al Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) por la actuación del juez <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/juan-carlos-peinado-garcia/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/juan-carlos-peinado-garcia/">Juan Carlos Peinado</a> cuando lo interrogó como testigo sobre la contratación de la asistenta de Begoña Gómez, la esposa del presidente del Gobierno, desgranan un total de 19 “irregularidades” que el ministro atribuye al juez. Las denuncias, recogidas en cinco cartas enviadas entre junio de 2025 y abril de 2026 a la presidenta del CGPJ, Isabel Perelló, recogen también el clima de alta tensión que rodeó la cita antes, durante e incluso después de la declaración (Bolaños insinúa que Peinado intentó que el Tribunal Supremo le imputara en represalia por quejarse ante el CGPJ). Con estos cinco escritos, a los que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS, el titular de Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes reclamó al Consejo que sancionara a Peinado apelando a la necesidad de “preservar el prestigio y la reputación” de la judicatura española. Pero el órgano de gobierno de los jueces <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-28/el-poder-judicial-envia-al-tsj-de-madrid-dos-investigaciones-al-juez-peinado-por-dos-posibles-faltas-de-desconsideracion-y-retraso.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-28/el-poder-judicial-envia-al-tsj-de-madrid-dos-investigaciones-al-juez-peinado-por-dos-posibles-faltas-de-desconsideracion-y-retraso.html">descartó el 28 de julio esa posibilidad y archivó las quejas de Bolaños</a> al considerar que, si bien algunas decisiones del magistrado pueden ser “discutibles”, no merecen reproche disciplinario.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-05/las-19-quejas-de-bolanos-sobre-peinado-que-el-cgpj-archivo-censuro-mi-expresion-facial-y-me-prohibio-sonreir.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Las 19 quejas de Bolaños sobre Peinado que el CGPJ archivó: “Censuró mi expresión facial y me prohibió sonreír”

articles.body: <p>El juez de la Audiencia Nacional José Luis Calama sigue la pista al capital venezolano que se ha aportado a la aerolínea Plus Ultra. Para ello, ha encargado a la Unidad de Delincuencia Económica y Fiscal (UDEF) de la Policía Nacional que realice un “estudio exhaustivo” sobre “la evolución de la propiedad del capital social” de la compañía, que permanece bajo el foco en el marco de una investigación sobre una supuesta trama de tráfico de influencias —<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-05-19/zapatero-imputado-por-blanqueo-de-capitales-en-el-caso-plus-ultra.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-05-19/zapatero-imputado-por-blanqueo-de-capitales-en-el-caso-plus-ultra.html">presuntamente liderada por el expresidente del Gobierno José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero</a>― para conseguir el rescate público de 53 millones de euros tras la pandemia.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/el-juez-pide-a-la-udef-un-estudio-exhaustivo-sobre-el-capital-venezolano-en-plus-ultra.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La estrategia fallida en Ceuta se ha unido estos días a lo que ya compartían el eurodiputado Alvise Pérez, el agitador Vito Quiles, el líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, y el grupo neonazi Núcleo Nacional. Desde que el pasado jueves <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/ceuta/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/ceuta/">se produjera el acceso masivo de migrantes a la ciudad</a>, las distintas facciones de la ultraderecha pusieron a funcionar su maquinaria para aprovecharlo como gasolina en sus planteamientos antiinmigración. Alvise Pérez trató de calentar los ánimos durante el fin de semana reclamando el “Estado de Sitio y la activación urgente de la Armada” ante la entrada de migrantes, y anunció que esperaba que “10.000 españoles venidos de la península” se trasladaran a la ciudad autónoma junto a él. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/esto-no-es-torre-pacheco-la-estrategia-fallida-de-la-ultraderecha-en-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/YIJJFYVUQVFPNHBNZRULS57NPQ.jpg?auth=056fa1f8121d2f9c81b82acaf0bf477fcd758d85b37534ddc2192d0359669cf8" width="5605" height="3793" alt="El líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, el domingo en Ceuta. articles.body: <p>Diecisiete migrantes han muerto en una patera que llevaba 15 días a la deriva y que<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-08-28/el-impulso-de-la-ruta-migratoria-de-argelia-a-baleares-mantiene-en-vilo-a-las-autoridades.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-08-28/el-impulso-de-la-ruta-migratoria-de-argelia-a-baleares-mantiene-en-vilo-a-las-autoridades.html"> trataba de alcanzar las costas de Baleares</a> con un total de 19 personas a bordo. Según ha informado la Delegación del Gobierno en Baleares, los dos únicos supervivientes de la travesía han explicado a Salvamento Marítimo tras ser rescatados que la embarcación partió de las costas del norte de África con las 19 personas, y que, salvo los dos supervivientes, fueron falleciendo a lo largo de las dos semanas que permanecieron a la deriva. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/mueren-al-menos-17-migrantes-al-tratar-de-alcanzar-las-costas-de-baleares.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/LRRS62XLQZAIPDFW5YEBC2VPJQ.JPG?auth=f70257abb0b800506c26990e9f203855cd1da009da77241cc9f4b3df93d5b76c" width="6000" height="4000" alt="Cientos de personas esperan en la frontera entre España y Marruecos"></img><p>La Moncloa ha destituido con carácter fulminante a la funcionaria responsable de comunicación del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DSN). El cese se produjo el pasado viernes, a través de una llamada telefónica, ya que la afectada se encontraba de vacaciones, después de que publicara a primera hora de la mañana una alerta en la web del DSN en la que informaba, citando fuentes del Ministerio del Interior, de que 49.000 inmigrantes habían entrado irregularmente en Ceuta. La alerta, que fue borrada poco después de difundirse y ya no aparece en la web del DSN, supuso el primer reconocimiento oficial de la dimensión que había tomado la irrupción masiva de inmigrantes en la ciudad española del norte de África, aunque la cifra se haya disparado posteriormente por encima de los 60.000. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-03/cese-fulminante-de-un-cargo-de-seguridad-nacional-por-informar-de-la-entrada-de-49000-inmigrantes-en-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Cese fulminante de un cargo de Seguridad Nacional por informar de la entrada de 49.000 inmigrantes en Ceuta

articles.body: <p>Si Ceuta <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-03/vallas-de-obra-para-cerrar-las-calles-y-batidas-para-ahuyentar-a-los-migrantes-que-se-resisten-a-dejar-ceuta-todavia-quedan.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-03/vallas-de-obra-para-cerrar-las-calles-y-batidas-para-ahuyentar-a-los-migrantes-que-se-resisten-a-dejar-ceuta-todavia-quedan.html">quiere o no recuperar la normalidad, tanto da</a>. Nada es ni remotamente normal. Cinco días después de la entrada a nado de más de 60.000 migrantes, la ciudad se ha partido en dos. De un lado, las zonas más céntricas en las que la fuerte presencia policial ha conseguido una aparente tranquilidad cosmética, una custodia que permite a los turistas volver a las calles que hace solo dos días recorrían centenares de migrantes. El Ejército les mantiene fuera de esa especie de zona de exclusión no oficial, pero evidente. El Gobierno cifra en 2.500 las personas que siguen en la ciudad después de haber pasado irregularmente la frontera estos días.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-03/calma-tensa-en-ceuta-cinco-dias-despues-de-la-entrada-masiva-de-inmigrantes.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El juez Juan Carlos Peinado ha devuelto a la Fiscalía Europea la pieza separada que abrió el pasado junio dentro de la causa impulsada contra Begoña Gómez, esposa del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, para <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-19/el-juez-peinado-abre-una-nueva-linea-de-investigacion-en-el-caso-contra-begona-gomez-con-dos-delitos-mas.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-19/el-juez-peinado-abre-una-nueva-linea-de-investigacion-en-el-caso-contra-begona-gomez-con-dos-delitos-mas.html">investigar al empresario Juan Carlos Barrabés por presunta prevaricación y fraude a los intereses de la Unión Europea</a>. En un auto, al que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS, el instructor ha dejado en manos del órgano europeo la investigación que se centraba en <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-26/la-uco-ve-arbitrariedad-en-las-adjudicaciones-de-redes-que-investiga-peinado-barrabes-es-la-buena-y-las-otras-han-de-bajar-si-o-si.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-26/la-uco-ve-arbitrariedad-en-las-adjudicaciones-de-redes-que-investiga-peinado-barrabes-es-la-buena-y-las-otras-han-de-bajar-si-o-si.html">un contrato de 4 millones de euros adjudicado en 2021 por la compañía pública Red.es</a> a una unión temporal de empresas (UTE) formada por Innova Next —propiedad de Barrabés— y la consultora KPMG. Este expediente fue supuestamente financiado con fondos comunitarios Feder.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-04/el-juez-peinado-devuelve-a-la-fiscalia-europea-la-investigacion-a-barrabes-por-presunto-fraude-en-una-adjudicacion-de-redes.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/jose-manuel-albares-bueno/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/jose-manuel-albares-bueno/">José Manuel Albares,</a> ha asegurado este lunes que España exigirá mañana en la reunión de ministros del Interior de la UE la solidaridad de los socios europeos ante la crisis de Ceuta y ha cargado contra algunos países, como Italia, que han anunciado l<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-31/bruselas-y-berlin-reclaman-el-retorno-rapido-a-marruecos-de-los-migrantes-que-han-cruzado-la-frontera-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-31/bruselas-y-berlin-reclaman-el-retorno-rapido-a-marruecos-de-los-migrantes-que-han-cruzado-la-frontera-en-ceuta.html">a suspensión del acuerdo Schengen de libre circulación de personas no europeas con España </a>por la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en la ciudad española del norte de África. “Vamos a exigir la solidaridad a todos los Estados de la UE”, ha dicho Albares a TVE, en sus primeras declaraciones desde que estalló la crisis el pasado jueves.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-03/albares-exige-la-solidaridad-de-los-socios-europeos-con-ceuta-y-carga-contra-meloni.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: (ACN) El brot de pesta porcina africana ha impactat directament en les entitats excursionistes de l’entorn de Collserola , que han hagut de fer mans i mànigues per mantenir la seva activitat amb propostes alternatives , lluny de les que solien oferir a través dels camins i corriols del parc. El Centre Excursionista de Catalunya (CEC), a més, alerta que les restriccions han fet caure a la meitat els infants que participen en els seus casals a Barcelona. Per això, reclamen la reobertura gradual del parc i s’ofereixen a participar-hi si cal fer controls o establir recorreguts segurs. També et pot interessar Quatre mesos sense Collserola: no es preveuen flexibilitzacions, almenys, fins a la tardor Queralt Gómez Cuberes 4 minuts de lectura Impacte de les restriccions El Centre Excursionista de Catalunya tenia com una de les seves activitats més recurrents els entrenaments per Collserola . Anaven des de Pedralbes fins a Mundet i també a Sant Cugat, però fa nou mesos que han de buscar alternatives als espais verds de la ciutat: “Són parcs i jardins i se’ns queda curt” , explica Carla Grau, responsable de l’àrea d’infants del CEC. Una situació semblant viuen al Club Muntanyenc Sant Cugat, organitzadors d’una marxa nòrdica amb més de 200 participants. “No és el mateix sortir a caminar aquí al costat de casa que haver de desplaçar-nos en vehicle a altres llocs sense restriccions”, afegeix Regina Anadón, secretària general del club. B. Blau / A. Salazar (ACN) Els casals d’estiu , organitzats pel Centre Excursionista de Catalunya, també han notat l’impacte de les restriccions a Collserola. Segons apunten, el nombre de famílies apuntades ha caigut un 50 % . “Una de les nostres virtuts era poder fer excursions a Collserola , aquest any no ho hem tingut i moltes famílies s’han desapuntat”. També et pot interessar Municipis afectats per les prohibicions i restriccions pel brot de pesta porcina africana | MAPA Javier Arilla 3 minuts de lectura Un pla de reobertura Aquests vuit mesos de restriccions, diuen, han estat més durs que les limitacions de mobilitat per la covid, que “només es van allargar tres mesos”. Per tot plegat, el club de Sant Cugat reclama la reobertura del bosc de Volpelleres , que no es troba tocant al parc, i que es creïn camins segurs a Collserola per poder fer senderisme : “Ens oferim com a voluntaris per delimitar un trajecte que pot estar obert en certes hores i col·laborar amb l’Ajuntament, la policia, Protecció Civil o els Agents Rurals per fer traçats”, diu el president del Club Muntanyenc Sant Cugat, Jaume Llugany. En aquest mateix sentit es pronuncia el CEC, que reclama al govern una flexibilització de les restriccions i es mostra disposat a col·laborar per evitar l’expansió del brot de pesta amb mesures com ara netejar les sabates en entrar i sortir del parc i mantenir uns horaris d’accés . També et pot interessar Negocis de Vallvidrera agonitzen amb les restriccions per la pesta porcina: “Haurem de tancar” Montse Llorens 3 minuts de lectura Crítiques pel film rodat a Collserola Grau també reflecteix la indignació que han copsat dels seus socis davant dels permisos que es van donar per a la filmació de la pel·lícula The last druid , protagonitzada per Russell Crowe, en uns terrenys de l’Incasòl situats en medi natural a Sant Cugat del Vallès : “Genera molta frustració veure que una persona que està gravant una pel·lícula sí que hi pot entrar, però després nosaltres no ho puguem fer servir”. En aquesta mateixa línia es pronuncia el Club Muntanyenc Sant Cugat, que retreu la doble vara de mesurar. articles.body: El sensellarisme a la ciutat de Barcelona és una realitat que creix i, de retruc, s’estén a més espais . Fa poc més d’un any que els veïns de la Vila Olímpica i del Poblenou conviuen, dia a dia, amb els assentaments que s’han col·locat a la zona i que asseguren que cada vegada s’amplien més. De moment, hi ha espais que ja han quedat desallotjats, però hi ha zones, com la plaça dels Campions i la font del Cobi, on encara pernocten desenes de persones . També et pot interessar El síndic de greuges presentarà una prova pilot per acabar amb el sensellarisme Guillem González Claramunt 2 minuts de lectura Reclamen un sostre per a les persones que hi pernocten Una de les persones que hi viuen és l’Alex, un home rus que fa sis mesos que es va desplaçar cap aquí. Cada matí neteja la seva tenda de campanya i també l’entorn, perquè, diu, li agrada cuidar Barcelona. Però aquest interès per mantenir net el que és casa seva no és suficient per a un grup de veïns que expliquen que, des que han proliferat les tendes de campanya, la zona s’ha tornat més insalubre i insegura . De fet, han començat a penjar un cartell en alguns edificis del barri per denunciar que la situació ja és insostenible . Per l’Associació de Veïns de la Vila Olímpica, però, aquesta protesta no té en compte la vulnerabilitat d’aquestes persones. Jordi Giró, el president de l’entitat, recorda que és important mantenir l’espai públic en condicions, però que darrere “ hi ha un transfons social “. De fet, demana que si es desallotgen aquestes persones se’ls ofereixi un “sostre o destí”, perquè “ són veïns de la ciutat ” com la resta. També et pot interessar Amnistia i Quart Món sostenen que desallotjar l’assentament de la Sagrera “és desplaçar el problema” Núria Granados 2 minuts de lectura Espais cada vegada més marginals “Si no hi ha una alternativa, la gent no desapareix “, i això ho té clar Beatriz Fernández, directora d’Arrels Fundació. De fet, algunes de les persones que ara pernocten als assentaments del litoral són els mateixos que fa mesos ho feien a la Zona Franca abans de ser desallotjats. Per tant, l’entitat recorda que desallotjar-los només desplaça la problemàtica, però no aporta solucions reals. En paral·lel, Arrels també denuncia que cada vegada s’acoten més els espais on poden quedar-se les persones sense llar i que així perden “la poca xarxa que poden tenir”: “S’està limitant la subsistència d’aquests persones per a què? Perquè se’n vagin, però a on ?”. Fernández apunta que les seves destinacions cada vegada són més marginals , perquè són a les vores. És el cas de la ronda del Litoral , un espai on la imatge també s’està transformant: “S’està fent un desplaçament del centre als afores”. També et pot interessar Arrels demana una moratòria dels desallotjaments de persones que viuen al carrer a Barcelona Ester Magdaleno 1 minut de lectura El consistori assegura que quan s’intervé als assentaments es fa per diversos factors: per exemple, quan s’hi detecten problemes de salubritat o bé problemes de convivència amb el barri. La comissionada d’Acció Social, Sonia Fuertes, recorda que en tot cas sempre s’intenta acompanyar les persones després d’aquestes actuacions.

articles.body: (ACN) TMB farà una auditoria dels revestiments de tots els túnels del metro arran de l’incendi entre les estacions del Clot i Glòries de la línia L1 , que va deixar un balanç de prop de 140 ferits. Ho ha anunciat Xavier Flores , conseller delegat de TMB , que ha explicat que l’auditoria tindrà com a objectiu verificar que els materials normatius en cas de foc “no suposen un risc afegit”. Flores també ha avançat que qualsevol element que presenti “un comportament diferent” de l’esperat davant d’un incendi “serà substituït”. En aquest sentit, Flores ha reiterat que el revestiment impermeabilitzant que va cremar no es troba en cap altre tram de la xarxa. També et pot interessar Un incendi a la catenària de l’L1 obliga a evacuar el Clot i Glòries sense cap ferit de gravetat Núria Granados 2 minuts de lectura Més protocols de seguretat El conseller de TMB també ha afirmat que es reforçaran els protocols d’emergència amb més informació al passatge. A més dels missatges des de les cabines de conducció, una de les novetats serà la incorporació als trens de cartells amb consells de seguretat per orientar els usuaris davant d’una incidència. Es volen evitar situacions com les del dia de l’incendi , quan el passatge va obrir les portes amb el tirador d’emergència i això va provocar que el fum entrés a dins del comboi o que moltes persones sortissin a la zona de vies. També et pot interessar TMB investiga si el foc a l’L1 el va causar un material que no hi ha a cap altre túnel Arnau Vaqué 2 minuts de lectura Un revestiment col·locat el 2019 L’incident es va produir la tarda del 27 de juliol quan un comboi de la línia L1 que es dirigia de Clot cap a Glòries es va aturar al túnel per presència de foc i fum . L’incendi va començar en cremar un revestiment impermeabilitzant que es va col·locar el desembre del 2019 en el marc de les obres dels túnels viaris de Glòries . Segons el conseller delegat de TMB, el revestiment es va encendre després de desprendre-se’n una part pel pas continu de combois i fer contacte amb la catenària . “L’incendi va ser molt ràpid i també es va apagar de forma molt ràpida amb l’ajuda d’extintors portàtils”, ha recalcat Flores, que ha insistit que no hi ha cap altre revestiment amb aquest material a la xarxa de metro. articles.body: (Clàudia Rosas) Quan falten pocs dies per a l’ eclipsi solar , un dels moments més esperats de l’estiu d’aquest 2026, els oftalmòlegs redoblen els missatges de la importància de la prevenció . Mirar directament el sol, encara que sigui només uns segons, pot deixar seqüeles irreversibles a la vista . Jesús Díaz , especialista en retina de l’Hospital de Sant Pau, detalla quins danys pot provocar aquesta exposició, quins símptomes cal vigilar i com distingir unes ulleres homologades realment segures d’unes que no ho són. Alerta a la lesió que afecta la visió central El punt més vulnerable de l’ull és la màcula, la zona central de la retina . És allà on es concentra la capacitat de veure amb nitidesa i és allà on l’ exposició solar prolongada pot provocar una maculopatia solar. “Es tracta d’una lesió que afecta directament el teixit neuronal de la retina, un teixit que, un cop danyat, té una capacitat de regeneració molt limitada. En els casos més greus, la pèrdua de visió central que en resulta és irreversible “, explica Jesús Díaz. Per saber-ne més Ulleres per a l’eclipsi solar 2026: 7 consells per gaudir de l’esdeveniment amb els ulls protegits Jessica Moreno Cusac 3 minuts de lectura No hi ha risc zero Una pregunta habitual és si només uns segons de mirada directa ja poden causar danys. La resposta del doctor Díaz és clara: com més temps s’exposa l’ull, més risc hi ha, però el risc zero no existeix en cap cas . És precisament per això que els oftalmòlegs insisteixen tant en la protecció ocular i recomanen no mirar mai directament el sol , ni tan sols per una estona breu. Símptomes que triguen hores a aparèixer Les lesions que poden aparèixer per l’eclipsi solar poden tardar a donar senyals. Els primers símptomes solen trigar en manifestar-se, normalment entre 12 i 24 hores després de l’exposició. Es tracta d’alteracions en la percepció dels colors, visió borrosa i l’aparició d’un escotoma: una taca negra fixa al centre del camp visual que dificulta veure amb normalitat allò que abans es veia sense esforç. El missatge dels experts Precaució per a l’eclipsi solar: “És imprescindible anar ben protegits” Marina Sancho 2 minuts de lectura Prevenció abans que tractament Davant d’aquests símptomes, la recomanació és anar directament a urgències. Però Díaz remarca que la prioritat real no és el tractament, sinó la prevenció , perquè les opcions terapèutiques provades són escasses un cop la lesió ja s’ha produït. Aquesta prevenció és especialment important en els infants , amb qui cal estar molt atents perquè no mirin el sol pel marge de les ulleres, esquivant la zona de protecció. Com identificar unes ulleres homologades vàlides No totes les ulleres garanteixen una bona protecció. Per assegurar-se que ho fan, cal fixar-se en tres elements: que portin el segell de la Unió Europea , que hi hagi informació clara del fabricant i que compleixin la normativa ISO 12312-2 , el codi numèric que certifica que aquelles ulleres protegeixen efectivament la retina. articles.body: Aquest és l’últim estiu abans de la cursa frenètica de les eleccions municipals 2027 . I això implica que més d’un i de dos hauran de treballar enèrgicament perquè tot vagi com ha d’anar d’aquí a uns mesos… encara que sigui a costa de sacrificar les vacances. Aquesta introducció ja dona força pistes de la resposta a la gran pregunta: “ On estiuejarà Jordi Martí , president del Grup Municipal de Junts ?” Doncs sembla que Martí serà un dels que hauran de renunciar a la relaxació: no marxarà enlloc , es quedarà a Barcelona per seguir fent feina del grup juntaire a l’Ajuntament. Però amb un extra perquè, com que serà el candidat a les municipals , també li toca fer feina com a alcaldable: preparar visites, documents, propostes… També et pot interessar Eleccions municipals 2027 a Barcelona: data, candidats i llistes del 23-M | GUIA Neus Reig 3 minuts de lectura Feinejant tot l’agost Ara bé, Jordi Martí té sort que estarà distret perquè, a l’agost, Barcelona té infinitud d’actes públics grossos, que són un aparador meravellós perquè els polítics hi treguin el nas. Un servidor dona fe, per exemple, que a la Festa Major de Gràcia i a la Festa Major de Sants –entre guarniment i guarniment– sempre hi ha un moment perquè els polítics de tots els colors delectin els periodistes amb un canutasso [un altre dia ja parlarem d’aquest concepte] d’allò més festiu. I si entre tanta activitat encara queda temps per a una mica de descans, persones molt properes a Jordi Martí expliquen a betevé que “mirarà de gaudir d’ algun racó de la ciutat on normalment no pot anar”. articles.body: Cop policial al transport no autoritzat de passatgers en vehicles de transport amb conductor (VTC) . Un dispositiu conjunt entre els Mossos d’Esquadra i el Servei Català de Trànsit ha immobilitzat vuit VTC que circulaven a l’aeroport del Prat sense llicència o amb autoritzacions d’altres comunitats autònomes . Segons la policia catalana, els automòbils han estat detectats durant un dispositiu desplegat a l’aparcament de la Terminal 1 de l’aeroport . La policia catalana ha detallat que set dels vehicles han estat immobilitzats per falsedat documental en circular amb autoritzacions d’altres comunitats autònomes, mentre que el vuitè ho feia sense cap llicència , per la qual cosa transportava els viatgers il·legalment. Per treballar a Barcelona, els VTC necessiten obligatòriament una llicència o autorització expedida per la Generalitat de Catalunya o l’Àrea Metropolitana de Barcelona (AMB). articles.body: La  previsió  del temps  per a aquest dimecres, 5 d’agost, indica un temps molt tranquil . El sol s’imposarà de manera clara a Barcelona i rodalia i només s’esperen alguns núvols d’evolució a l’entorn del Montseny, però difícilment amb pluja . Calor i xafogor intenses, fins i tot més que dimarts. Durant la tarda es podran formar núvols al prelitoral i, molt especialment, al massís del Montseny , tot i que sense que s’hi esperi pluja. La temperatura serà més alta i es podran tocar els 35 ºC al prelitoral i superar amb molta facilitat els 30 ºC a Barcelona. Continuaran la calor i la xafogor molt intenses les 24 hores del dia. articles.body: El Barça ha fet oficial el fitxatge de Kerolin Nicoli. És una davantera brasilera, que pot ocupar qualsevol posició de l’atac, que té 26 anys i que arriba procedent del Manchester City . Signa fins al mes de juny de 2030. Ha arribat per deixar empremta. Benvinguda, Kerolin! pic.twitter.com/cRm8G30eiE — FC Barcelona Femení (@FCBfemeni) August 4, 2026 El club blaugrana abonarà entre un i un milió i mig d’euros al Manchester City per incorporar la internacional brasilera, una xifra que supera qualsevol inversió feta fins ara pel conjunt femení del Barça. L’operació també es converteix en la venda més elevada que ha tancat el conjunt anglès i en un dels traspassos més importants del futbol femení europeu. Qui és Kerolin Nicoli? Amb 26 anys, Kerolin arriba al Barça després de consolidar-se com una de les davanteres més desequilibrants del panorama internacional . Destaca per la seva velocitat, el desbordament i la capacitat de generar superioritats en l’un contra un. La gran explosió de Nicoli va ser als Estats Units després de tres temporades al North Carolina Courage . De fet, va ser escollida millor jugadora de la NWSL el 2023 . La seva bona actuació li va valer per fer el pas a la Premier League amb el Manchester City . Abans de ser als Estats Units, també va militar a les files del Madrid CF. La brasilera és l’aposta del Barça per reforçar una línia ofensiva que aquest estiu ha perdut peces importants.
